question: A 55-year-old woman, 5 days post total hip replacement, develops a swollen, erythematous, tender left calf. Duplex ultrasound confirms a proximal deep vein thrombosis (DVT) extending to the popliteal vein. What is the most appropriate initial management?

answers.text: Start therapeutic anticoagulation (LMWH or direct oral anticoagulant) and arrange graduated compression stockings

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Confirmed proximal DVT requires therapeutic anticoagulation to prevent propagation and pulmonary embolism. LMWH (e.g., enoxaparin) or a DOAC (e.g., rivaroxaban) are the preferred agents; compression stockings reduce post-thrombotic syndrome. Inferior vena cava filter is reserved for contraindications to anticoagulation.

answers.text: Immediate surgical thrombectomy to remove the clot

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Surgical venous thrombectomy is rarely performed for DVT in modern practice. Anticoagulation is the primary treatment; catheter-directed thrombolysis is reserved for massive DVT with threatened limb viability (phlegmasia cerulea dolens).

answers.text: Observation only with bed rest and leg elevation, as DVT usually resolves spontaneously after hip replacement

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Proximal DVT carries a significant risk of pulmonary embolism — approximately 20-40% of untreated proximal DVTs embolise. Active anticoagulation is mandatory.

answers.text: Emergency pulmonary angiography to exclude concurrent pulmonary embolism before starting any treatment

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. In a haemodynamically stable patient with confirmed proximal DVT, therapeutic anticoagulation should be started immediately without waiting for pulmonary imaging. CT pulmonary angiography is obtained if there are clinical features of PE.

overallFeedback.feedback: Proximal DVT after orthopaedic surgery = therapeutic anticoagulation (not observation, not routine surgery). LMWH or DOAC prevents clot propagation and pulmonary embolism, which can be fatal.
Well done. Confirmed proximal DVT = start therapeutic anticoagulation immediately (LMWH or DOAC) to prevent PE. Surgery and thrombolysis are reserved for special circumstances.
